title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real / production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition; results, execution accounting, representative artifacts, and analysis logs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement. Our principal contribution is the concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and empirical studies establish several facts that motivate our design. First, intent-to-configuration pipelines using LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled and emulation-style setups, but reported results typically require downstream checking or human oversight [1],[5]. Second, deterministic verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (Batfish evolution, header-space and model-checking methods) are mature for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[6]. Third, generate–verify–repair and program-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, though semantic and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [4],[7]. Finally, security analyses of prompt-injection highlight the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines because adaptive retrieval-based threats remain an open problem [8].

This study differs from prior work in three ways: (i) it uses a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates; (ii) it reports deterministic provider-call reconciliation to show stage-level accounting (shared initial generation vs repair); and (iii) it archives full validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 as a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration fixed the single-repair policy, exclusion and contamination detectors, the analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget (maximum_model_calls = 500). The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede and is archived in the evidence bundle.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider accounting. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one initial generation call was produced per intent and that same candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call accounting reconciles hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} (see deterministic reconciliation artifacts in the archive). This mapping demonstrates that the executed comparison measures only the marginal validator+repair effect on identical model outputs.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label. Tasks exercised realistic workflow constraints (make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe-access transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. The full task manifest and representative task payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model and pipeline configuration. The declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini (recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). For each intent one shared initial generation call was executed. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, verifying required_sequence ordering, evaluating workflow-group constraints, and computing a final_state snapshot to compare to expected_final_state. When the validator returned valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one template-driven automated repair (syntactic and ordering fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration free-form repair or human escalation was permitted by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and handling of failures. Exclusion rules removed items failing vendor-parsers that prevented deterministic verification or containing credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from primary analysis and treated in sensitivity analyses. In the executed confirmatory partition no episodes were excluded or flagged: complete_pair_count = 250 and contamination summary is empty. On LLM API call failure the preregistration allowed one immediate retry; the execution manifest records no failed host calls.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729. Secondary and sensitivity analyses were defined but are reported as exploratory.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw counts. Execution completed the confirmatory synthetic/emulation partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation + 1 repair). Provider-call accounting reconciles to hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table observed is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference and uncertainty. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric analysis artifacts, contingency CSVs, and bootstrap parameters are archived in the evidence bundle.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair trace. Validator traces for passed episodes report parsed_command_count and required_command_count matching the task payload's required_sequence for typical medium/hard tasks (examples archived; see execution/scoring entries). Only one automated repair call occurred and converted the single failing baseline candidate into a guarded pass; the repair trace describing the template-driven syntactic/order fix is archived with the episode artifact.
sections.discussion:
Operational meaning. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the maximum verifier-detected improvement under these pipeline and task-scope conditions.

Artifact-grounded explanations. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed guarded gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced task ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents (see raw_results); and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshots) and does not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or emergent cross-device interactions.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and therefore reduced power to detect small absolute improvements; the observed paired-bootstrap CI is the most practically informative output.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: sensitivity to prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol-level behavior. External validity: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; community and production-like partitions in the preregistration were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.

Operational implications and caution. These results indicate that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This should not be generalized to production or adversarial settings: richer validators, multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, or production heterogeneity could materially change the benefit calculus. The archived artifacts permit reanalysis under alternate validator encodings, repair templates, or treated partitions.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and artifacts: declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair).

Preregistration and immutable prompt references: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Archive pointer: the full execution and analysis evidence bundle (manifests, raw model responses, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis CSVs referenced in the paper) is archived under the run's execution manifest (full_hash_manifest_path: execution/execution_manifest.json) within the evidence bundle. The paper body omits per-file paths and per-artifact full hashes for concision; the immutable preregistration SHA and the immutable master-prompt path+SHA above are provided as required by the track.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
